[Testing] This connection-failure test assumes port 9999 is unused. If another process is listening there, the request may succeed or fail differently, making the test environment-dependent. Use `PortUtils.UNUSABLE_PORT` for both client URLs in this test, as the repository's connection-failure tests do.

This issue also appears on line 403 of the same file.

threads.body: Structured-output requests bypass this instrumentation. In OpenAI SDK 2.20.1, within the declared supported version range, `create` and `createStreaming` also accept `StructuredResponseCreateParams<T>`. These overloads fail this parameter-type check and are invoked on the raw delegate, so their internal calls with `rawParams()` never re-enter the proxy. Using the frozen wrappers with that SDK, ordinary requests exported one span each, but structured synchronous/asynchronous requests and streams all exported zero. Route the structured overloads through the instrumented path in both service wrappers, preserving their structured return type, and cover them against a supporting SDK version.

replies.body:
Fixed in ff6c3aa. Both Responses wrappers now route the `StructuredResponseCreateParams` overloads of `create` and `createStreaming` through instrumentation via `rawParams()`, and sync and async `create` keep the SDK's structured return types. The library compiles against 1.1.0, so `ResponseServiceOverloads` resolves those types once through cached method handles, like `ChatCompletionEventsHelper` does.

The no-params `create()`, `create(RequestOptions)` and matching `createStreaming` overloads from 2.x had the same problem. They use the same instrumented path now.

`structured`, `structuredStream`, `withoutParams` and `withoutParamsStream` cover all four client modes under `testLatestDeps`, with and without `RequestOptions`. `structured` also checks the parsed output. Without the fix, none of them produce a Responses span.

threads.body: Calling `withOptions(...)` drops the Responses instrumentation. On SDK 2.20.1, `client.responses().withOptions(b -> b.maxRetries(0)).create(params)` reaches this fallback, which returns the delegate's unwrapped `ResponseServiceAsync`; the synchronous wrapper has the same problem. Real requests through both modified services succeeded but exported zero spans, while the same requests without `withOptions` exported one each. Intercept this service-view method and wrap its returned service with the same instrumenter in both wrappers so per-service option overrides retain telemetry.

Fixed in ff6c3aa. Both Responses wrappers now wrap the service returned by `withOptions(...)` with the same instrumenter. The `withOptions` test uses `maxRetries(0)` in all four client modes under `testLatestDeps`. It asserts the Responses span and fails without the fix.

`withOptions(...)` on both clients and on the chat, chat completions and embeddings wrappers has the same gap, so `client.withOptions(...).responses()` is still uninstrumented. Chat completions also misses its structured overloads. I'll fix those in a follow-up PR unless you'd rather have them here.

threads.body: [Testing] Optional: this assertion checks only the response ID, so missing model, finish-reason, or token attributes—and unexpected attributes—would go unnoticed on the `withOptions()` path. Use `hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly` with the complete expected attributes, following `.github/instructions/java-tests.instructions.md:135–137` and `basic()` above.

[Testing] Please add a regression test for an application stream consumer throwing. `streamFailure()` covers SDK parsing errors, but not this guard's distinction between SDK and application failures. Throw from a synchronous `forEach` or `map`, then close the response and assert that the same exception propagates and exactly one span is exported without a client error. This protects the error classification shared by Chat and Responses streams.

replies.body: Added `streamConsumerError` in e22ad25: it throws from a sync `forEach`, closes the response, and asserts the same exception propagates and the one Responses span ends without an error status, exception or `error.type`. Without the `inAction` guard, both sync modes fail.

threads.body: [General] Set `GenAiSchemaUrls.SCHEMA_URL` on the Responses builder, as the chat and embeddings builders do. `GenAiAttributesExtractor` does not supply a schema URL, so these spans, metrics, and exception logs otherwise omit the adopted GenAI schema. This also puts Responses measurements in a different instrumentation scope from the existing GenAI metric streams.

[General] In SDK 1.1.0 and 4.91.0, connection or HTTP failures can complete `onCompleteFuture()` exceptionally before `subscribe()` is called. Awaiting that failure without subscribing leaves the Responses span and metrics unfinished; closing afterward ends the span without recording the error. Register a completion callback on the SDK stream when creating the listener so failures are recorded independently of subscription, using the existing atomic guard to prevent duplicate completion.
